standards.label: Understand the concept of a ratio; describe a ratio relationship.
Understand unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b.
Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world problems.
Make tables of equivalent ratios; plot on the coordinate plane.
Solve unit rate problems including unit pricing and constant speed.
Find a percent of a quantity; solve percent problems.
Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units.
Divide fractions by fractions; interpret quotients.
Fluently divide multi-digit numbers (standard algorithm).
Fluently add, subtract, multiply, divide multi-digit decimals.
GCF, LCM, and distributive property factoring.
Understand positive and negative numbers in real-world contexts.
Understand a rational number as a point on the number line.
Opposite signs of numbers; opposite of the opposite.
Signs of ordered pairs; reflections across axes.
Position integers and rationals on number line and coordinate plane.
Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.
Interpret inequality statements about relative position.
Write, interpret, and explain ordering statements in context.
Understand absolute value as distance from zero; magnitude.
Distinguish comparisons of absolute value from order statements.
Solve problems by graphing points in all four quadrants; distance.
Write and evaluate numerical expressions with whole-number exponents.
Write, read, and evaluate expressions with letters for numbers.
Write expressions for verbal descriptions.
Identify parts of an expression (terms, factors, coefficients).
Evaluate expressions at specific values; use formulas.
Apply properties to generate equivalent expressions.
Identify when two expressions are equivalent.
Understand solving an equation/inequality as a question of truth.
Use variables to represent numbers; write expressions for problems.
Solve real-world one-step equations x+p=q and px=q.
Write inequalities of the form x>c or x<c; represent on number line.
Solve problems in context by writing and solving one-variable inequalities and interpreting solution sets on a number line.
Represent relationships between dependent and independent variables.
Area of triangles, quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing/decomposing.
Volume of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths.
Draw polygons in the coordinate plane; find side lengths.
Represent 3-D figures with nets; find surface area.
Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability.
Use the language of probability (likely, unlikely, certain, impossible) to describe likelihood and anticipate variability in data.
Understand a data distribution: center, spread, and shape.
Measures of center summarize with one number; variation with one number.
Display data on number lines: dot plots, histograms, box plots.
Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context.
Report the number of observations.
Describe the nature of the attribute and units of measurement.
Give measures of center and variability (IQR, MAD); describe pattern.
Relate choice of center/variability measure to data shape and context.
